what_happened: Found the required 11-phase-at-phase-0-vs-5-cycle-budget fixture AND its phase-10-of-11-with-budget-remaining counter-fixture as real, already-archived history (task 411's own metrics.jsonl/issues.jsonl) rather than needing to construct synthetic cases; also found a second real hard-mode instance (task 328, 20-phase plan, 18 implement cycles, every single cycle advancing exactly +1 phase with zero deviation) confirming the architecture doc's per-phase-dispatch claim as an observed near-exact 1:1 ratio. A threshold of remaining_phases > remaining_cycles*2 (base) / *1 (hard) is grounded directly in this measured data and satisfies both required fixtures without special-casing.

orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's budget-remaining is a SHARED BATCH-WIDE POOL (batch_cycle_budget minus sum of all tasks' cycle_counts), not a per-task-isolated counter -- the dispatch description's own 'task resumed at phase 10 of 11 with 4 cycles left' framing is only the batch-of-one special case of this pool. A plan/implement phase that naively implements a per-task subtraction instead of reading the pool would silently disagree with the mechanism that actually enforces MAX_CYCLES.

validate-artifact.sh's advisory cross-phase ceiling-consistency check false-positived on statistical prose in a Scope Hypothesis line: the phrase '92 of 155 run_sut call sites' was parsed as a per-phase quantity estimate against a nonsensical '0-of ceiling', emitting 'sum to 92 ... past the cited 0-of ceiling'. Rephrased the clause to drop the N-of-M shape. Separately, suite_selection_select returns a LARGER set when several paths are passed in one call than the union of per-path calls, so a Tier Justification built from per-path runs under-named four suites until corrected.
